title: Throughput-Tail Sensitivity Matrix (May 2026) - draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is an informal benchmark draft exploring how tail (p99/p999/p9999) latency behaves as we push throughput and change scheduling knobs. Goal: give product/ops a simple sensitivity matrix to inform SLOs and recommended defaults for Hosted API and Dedicated pools.

High-level takeaway (short):
- P50/P95 are relatively stable across moderate batching changes, but p99+ and p9999 blow up non-linearly once queueing/GC/microburst interactions occur.
- Small batch sizes + KV-prefetching dramatically reduce p999 tails for prefix-heavy workloads.
- Quantization reduces median token latency 15-25% on a40-like instances but has mixed effect on p999 when memory pressure moves to host and swaps occur.
- Cost per 1M tokens and tail latency tradeoffs are visible: cheapest configuration is often not viable for strict p999 SLOs.

Experiment matrix (configs tested):
- Models: open-7b, redwood-v1-small (fp16 baseline)
- Hardware: A40 (40GB), L4 (48GB), 1xA100-80GB (single GPU), 4xA100 (multi-GPU for throughput)
- Quantization: fp16 baseline, 4-bit (q4f16), int8-fused
- Batching: batch windows of 0ms (no batching), 5ms, 20ms, 50ms
- KV-cache: none (stateless), on-demand, prefetch (prefix caching)
- Sequence scenarios: short (prompt 32 tokens, gen 16), medium (prompt 128, gen 128), long prefix (prompt 1024, gen 256)
- Traffic: steady-at-target-RPS and bursty (ramp to 3x for 3s every 30s)

Key metric definitions used in tables:
- throughput_req_s: request completions per second (inference requests finished)
- tok/s: effective output tokens/sec across cluster
- p50/p95/p99/p999 latency (ms): end-to-end request time for generation completion
- cost_per_1M_tokens_usd: rough hosted cost estimate (in token units) using current price model for this draft (internal estimate)

Representative results (ASCII table):
Note: values are median of 3 runs unless otherwise noted. This table focuses on the medium sequence scenario and a single-A40 endpoint.

Batch-window | batching | throughput_req_s | tok/s | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | p999 (ms) | cost_per_1M_tokens_usd
------------ | -------- | ---------------- | ----- | -------- | -------- | -------- | --------- | ---------------------
0ms (no)     | no       | 120              | 12k   | 95       | 180      | 320      | 980       | 34.2
5ms          | yes      | 150              | 15k   | 112      | 210      | 520      | 2300      | 26.8
20ms         | yes      | 210              | 21k   | 160      | 320      | 900      | 4800      | 19.1
50ms         | yes      | 260              | 26k   | 230      | 520      | 1800     | 12000     | 15.4

Observations from table:
- Increasing batching increases throughput and decreases cost_per_1M_tokens, but p99/p999 get worse quickly.
- Even modest 5ms window increased p99 from 320->520ms: small windowing can introduce queueing amplification under bursty tails.

Tail breakdown by KV-cache behavior (medium sequence, A40, 20ms batch window):
Scenario       | p99 (ms) | p999 (ms)
---------------|---------|---------
stateless      | 900     | 4800
on-demand KV  | 620     | 2000
prefetch KV    | 340     | 720

Notes:
- Prefetching prefixes (for conversational workloads where user messages are long) reduces p999 by ~6.6x vs stateless in this setup. This is a high-leverage knob for chat products.
- Prefetching cost: memory footprint increases per-session, raising needed GPU memory. For A40 this was OK, for L4 we saw ~12% OOM rate unless eviction thresholds are tuned.

Quantization effects (open-7b, medium seq, 20ms batching):
Mode   | tok/s | p50 (ms) | p99 (ms) | p999 (ms) | notes
-------|-------|----------|---------|----------|------
fp16   | 21k   | 160      | 900     | 4800     | baseline
q4f16  | 24k   | 130      | 980     | 7200     | better median, worse extreme tails due to memory compaction/paging
int8   | 27k   | 120      | 1020    | 6400     | highest throughput but sensitive to batching policy

Interpretation: quant helps latency median and throughput, but tail behavior is brittle when memory pressure causes host<->device movement (esp on smaller GPU types). For strict p999 SLOs (>1000ms target) we should be conservative about quant configs on smaller instance types.

Microburst / bursty traffic profile finding:
- Under a repeating 3s 3x burst every 30s traffic pattern, p999 spikes are much higher (2–6x) than steady ramps even when average RPS matches. The scheduler (time-slicing vs token-slicing) matters a lot: token-slicing with preemption reduced p999 by ~30% in our token-latency-aware scheduler experiment.

Cost vs Tail tradeoff heatmap (qualitative):
- Cheapest setups (large batching, quant) -> high p999 risk (bad for strict SLO customers).
- Middle ground (moderate batching 5–20ms, KV prefetch on warm sessions) -> 2x cost vs cheapest but p999 within 800–1200ms which is acceptable for many interactive apps.
- Premium config (small batches, prefetch, overprovision 20%) -> 3-4x cost but p999 < 300ms consistently for medium seq.

Sample recommendations (for product and Dedicated defaults):
1) Hosted API default: medium-throughput profile
   - batch window: 20ms, kv-mode: on-demand, quant: fp16 by default, autoscale headroom: +30%
   - SLO target: p95 < 400ms, p999 < 2s (explainable in SLA as "best-effort for p999")
2) Low-latency premium tier (enterprise):
   - batch window: 0–5ms, kv-mode: prefetch, quant: conservative (fp16 or q4 only on large GPUs), reserve dedicated pools
   - SLO guarantee: p99 < 250ms, p999 < 400ms
3) Cost-optimized (background/batch jobs):
   - batch window: 50ms+, aggressive quant, stateless ok, recommend pre-warmed multi-GPU cluster

Operational notes / TODOs:
- Need more runs on multi-GPU (4xA100) configs with mixed request sizes — current results only single-GPU or scale-out emulations.
- Re-test L4 memory eviction heuristics when KV prefetch enabled; file a follow-up to infra to tune GC and eviction thresholds (RI-2137).
- Add token-slicing scheduler experiment to CI microbench harness and capture p999 on redistributed workload.
- Build a one-pager for sales explaining the three profiles (default, premium, cost-optimized) with simple cost vs latency visuals.

Unresolved questions / open items:
- What is the right p999 SLO for Hosted? Product suggested "best-effort" for p999 but ops would prefer a numeric guidance.
- How to communicate tail variance to customers (charting p99 vs p999 in console)?
- Are we comfortable recommending quantization for Dedicated customers by default, or should we gate based on GPU family?

Notes to self (raw):
- include raw harness ids and raw logs in the Confluence page for reproducibility.
- baseline price numbers used here are internal, will update with official pricing table before posting.

Appendix: short experiment config snippet (text form)
- harness: runtime-perf-v2
- run_id: tail-sens-may18-2026-01
- model: open-7b
- hardware: a40-single
- concurrency target: 210 req/s for medium seq in batched runs
- measurements: 3x runs, 95% CI shown where anomalous

Link references:
- RI ticket with KV prefetch prototype: https://linear.app/RUN/issue/RI-2137
- runtime PR for token-slicing scheduler: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
- placeholder Confluence page id: CONFSYS-9842

End of draft.

(Most of this is rough notes — want feedback on which configs to bake into the public Synthetic Bench page and which to keep internal.)
